content.thinking:
I'll plan out the whole module carefully in one pass, aiming for a hunched swamp troll around 2.6 meters tall in a Warcraft-inspired style, with a skeleton built from hips as root through spine, neck, head, jaw, and simplified arms with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and a fist-like hand instead of detailed fingers.

Mapping out the joint chains now: spine as a catmull curve from hips upward with named segments ending in a chest tip, then a neck chain continuing forward and up into a head joint, with a separate jaw joint parented to the head. I'm keeping the posture hunched by angling the head and spine forward and low to match the troll's silhouette.

For the body geometry, I'm sweeping a tube along the spine chain with varying elliptical radii to shape the big belly, offsetting the profile along the frame's normal so the torso bulges forward appropriately.

For the skin, I'm layering a swamp-green mottled paint with countershading for a lighter belly, then adding noise-based moss patches on upward-facing surfaces by checking the normal's y-component against a threshold.

Now I'm moving on to the arms, defining the shoulder joint position so I can chain the limb geometry using a catmull curve.

So 4 points with 4 names works, confirming the chain structure. I'm setting the shoulder joint parented to the chest/spine tip, with the arm positioned slightly off the chest bulk, and defining a tapering radius array for the sweep from shoulder down to hand.

Now I'm building out the hand geometry: a bulkier shoulder muscle, a scaled fist/palm shape at the wrist tip, and four finger capsules curving downward from the knuckles with slight spread and radius tapering toward claw-like tips.

For the legs, I'm planning the joint chain — hip, knee, ankle, and toe positions on each side — and sweeping a tube path through them so the leg thickens at the thigh and tapers toward the foot, treating the foot as the final segment of that same curve.

Checking the toe cap clearance confirms the sink is negligible, well within tolerance. For the hips I'm planning a sphere-based pelvis attached to the hip bone, then working out a belt using a torus geometry scaled into an ellipse and tilted to wrap around the hip joint as a cheap, robust alternative to a lathe skirt.

Settling on belt radius around 0.4 with a slightly thicker tube for visibility. For the loincloth I'll use extruded flat panels hanging from the hips bone, with a front panel reaching down past the thighs, painted with a leather-like pattern. Now moving to the head design: a heavy brow, jutting lower jaw, and tusks, attached at a neck joint.

I'm figuring out the coordinate system for positioning head features -- defining the neck's curved path ending near the head, then building a helper function that places points relative to the head using forward/up/left offsets so I can consistently position jaw, tusks, and brow without manual trig each time.

Continuing to work out the facial features: brow ridge, glowing eyes, muzzle and nose with nostrils, then the lower jaw geometry including underbite and curved tusk spikes sweeping upward from the jawbone with proper positioning.

Now I'm figuring out the mouth interior shading and small teeth boxes, then moving to the ears -- considering whether to extrude a flat outline or just use a simpler cone/spike shape swept back from the side of the head with a flattened elliptical cross-section.

For the mohawk, I'm planning a row of tapered blade shapes running along the cranium's centerline from forehead to neck, each extruded from a tuft outline and placed along an arc following the skull's curvature.

Attaching the front spikes to the head bone and the rear ones to the neck joint so they follow motion naturally, I'm building each blade as a sweep between base and tip with alternating dark red coloring.

Shaping blade dimensions...

Now I'm thinking about bone fetish decorations—a necklace of bones and small skull amulets, hanging bundles of bones and feathers on the belt, plus a shoulder trophy with spikes, and I'll need helper functions to build crossed bone bundles and simple skull shapes.

Working out the feather geometry orientation...

Now I'm planning the necklace as a curved pendant path draping across the chest, with points mapped around neck and chest area to form a hanging loop shape.

Rather than manually computing the front-chest point through tangent/normal math, it's simpler to just drape the necklace path onto the torso surface using the surface-draping tool with a small lift so it naturally sits above the chest geometry.

I'll sample points along the draped path to place hanging charms with a small downward offset, and position a larger central amulet near the midpoint of the necklace, slightly below and forward. I also want to give the torso a bigger, paunchy belly shape to match the troll's proportions.

I'm defining the torso's radius profile with widening shoulders and a rib-cage-like curve, but I need to check where the tube's rounded cap ends up relative to the neck and head so they don't overlap—adjusting the spine's top endpoint to keep the shoulders and neck placement sensible.

I'm placing the spine, neck, and head points, adding a trapezius hump sphere for the hunch, and totaling up head height plus a mohawk to land around 2.45-2.5m for the hunched troll's overall scale.

Now I'm positioning the shoulder joints separately from the torso's spine chain, setting shoulder muscle sphere size and placement to overlap the chest width, then starting the arm path from shoulder toward elbow.

Working out elbow, wrist, and hand-end coordinates to get long ape-like arm proportions, then shaping forearm muscle bulge with a tapering radii array across four keyframes, plus a separate upper-arm bulge sphere.

Setting up the arm chain with named joints and a tip pointer, then laying out leg joints from hip to knee to ankle to ball with their own radii taper, and starting on the foot bone structure.

Now I'm building out the feet: spherical foot masses with scaled geometry, plus three forward toes using small rods ending in claw spikes, sized and positioned so they rest correctly on the floor. I'm also starting to add a hand-painted gradient highlight to the skin shading for a stylized Warcraft look.

Fixing the smoothstep direction for the shadow blend. Then I want to scatter small wart spheres across torso and arm surfaces using the surface scatter helper, plus consider adding tribal paint stripes or tattoo decals on the torso for extra character detail.

For the tattoo, I'm placing a decal on the chest using a surface ray hit at a chosen azimuth and elevation, checking that the hit isn't null before applying. I'll draw a simple tribal glyph as an SVG texture and decide to keep it to just chest and maybe shoulder placement to avoid overdoing it.

Writing SVG decal...

For the eyes, I'm thinking small yellow glowing spheres with tiny black pupil spheres layered on top, using a glow effect on the yellow part for a fiery look against the flat-colored skin.

Still planning the tusks and bone fetishes with a bone-colored gradient shading from base to tip, then sketching out the jaw joint attachment relative to the head.

I'm now setting up the head geometry itself, placing the center point ahead of the neck joint, sizing the short thick neck radii, and beginning to lay out the cranium sphere and other head components as offsets from that center.

Continuing to add facial features like the brow ridge, eye sockets, and pupils, positioning them relative to the head center with appropriate colors and sizes.

Now I'm shaping the muzzle and nose region, placing nostrils and checking their offsets so they sit correctly on the snout, then starting work on the lower jaw geometry for the underbite.

Still building jaw and tusk shapes...

Adding a small tooth row of upward spikes along the jaw, then working out the ears—using a three-point curve from base to tip with a tapering radius, though I'm unsure how the tube orientation will handle a sideways-pointing shape and whether the cross-section ends up flat or round.

Going with a simple circular taper for the ear instead, and adding a small gold earring torus near the ear's midpoint, rotated to face sideways. Now I'm figuring out positions for the mohawk blades across the top of the cranium, spacing nine of them from front to back using a curved height profile.

Still working out mane blade placement...

I'm settling on hump sphere dimensions and parenting the blades to the chest bone, then shifting to color design: a saturated gradient mohawk running from dark magenta-red at the base to orange at the tips. Now I'm starting to plan the character's fetish accessories, beginning with a bone-and-skull necklace.

Planning the remaining fetishes: a belt with hanging bone bundles and a pouch, an animal skull shoulder pauldron with bone spikes on one side and a feather-bone bundle on the other, spiked wrist bracers, and skipping any hand-held item in favor of hanging totems from the belt instead. I'm setting up helper functions and color constants inside the build function before starting the skull geometry.

Writing skull geometry function...

Now I'm budgeting part counts across body regions—torso, limbs, head, mohawk, warts, fetishes—to stay under the 1000 part limit, then planning scattered warts and hanging moss tufts using surface hits on the torso, arms, head, and shoulder hump, with small SVG textures for the moss.

Scattering moss cards on the torso and hump surfaces, filtering hits by upward-facing normals, then adding mud staining near the feet and lower legs.

Now I'm shaping the loincloth as a leather panel with a scalloped bottom edge, carefully plotting the outline points on each side so the shape stays simple and non-crossing.

I need to figure out the belly's actual forward z-position to place the loincloth panels correctly, so I'll use a surface ray cast against the torso mesh to get the precise hit point rather than guessing a fixed offset.

For the belt itself, instead of a simple torus, I'm computing hip radii in both x and z directions via ray casts, then building a closed catmull-rom sweep around an ellipse centered between the front and back hits, giving a tube-shaped leather belt that actually conforms to the body.

I'm also planning accessories: a skull buckle positioned on the belt front, explicitly binding the belt sweep to the hips bone since no joint sits directly on the path, and a small hanging pouch at the left hip placed using the same side-ray hit distance.

For the shoulder, I'm adding a muscle sphere pauldron with an oversized skull mounted on top plus horn spikes, then sketching a rough diagonal bandolier path running from the left shoulder across the chest down to the right hip.

Rather than wrapping fully around the torso, I'll limit the drape to front-facing points so it hugs the visible surface naturally, then sweep a thin leather cord along that curve with hanging bones attached. I'm deciding to go with just the bandolier of tiny skulls and teeth as the single chest accessory rather than layering it with a separate necklace.

Now I'm positioning the wrist bracers, computing a cylinder aligned with the forearm direction from elbow to hand so it sits naturally at the wrist joint.

Still working out spike signatures...

Now I'm checking the bracer cylinder thickness against forearm radius at the wrist, then laying out the palm sphere scale and finger rod positions with skin-colored bones attached to the hand joint.

Still building hand details...

Now I'm setting up knuckle spheres with claw spikes in a dark bone color, positioning the thumb at the inner side angled toward the palm so the hand faces the body naturally, then moving to the pelvis sphere scaled and colored skin tone sitting at the hips with leg tops branching outward.

I'm checking the color budget stays under 64 by listing flat colors like bone, leather, gold, eye, claw, and feather tones — still comfortably within range. I'm writing a feather helper that extrudes a leaf shape along a bone direction with a paint function darkening a thin central vein stripe down the middle.

Now I'm setting up imports for the actual implementation file, pulling in THREE, the builder, frame, rng, catmull path utilities, and the paint helpers like countershade, gradient, mix, mottle, noise, and smoothstep, plus svg texture and glow kit, while double-checking whether the Joint type is actually exported from the skeleton module before importing it.

Building skeleton hierarchy...

Still writing jaw joint...

Now sketching the torso sweep, varying radius along the spine with a smoothstep taper and a sinusoidal shift so it bulges naturally through the middle.

Setting up ray-casting against the torso surface to find the belt's front and back z-positions at the correct height.

I'm reconsidering the pelvis sphere scale since it's redundant with the torso and could poke through the belt, so I'm shrinking it to tuck into the legs junction. Then I'm computing the belt's center and radii from the front/back/side ray hits and generating ten points around the loop at that height.

Next I'm sweeping a closed Catmull belt curve with leather coloring and bone attachment, adding gold studs along the path via an along-callback, and starting the loincloth front piece positioned just below belt height.

For the loincloth, I'm setting up a paint function to add a trim pattern — a darker red or gold band near the top edge and a leather base with grain texture across the middle, then mirroring the setup for a back panel on the opposite side.

Now I'm figuring out a small belt pouch on the left hip, positioning it based on a ray cast to find the body's edge, hanging it from the belt line with a box shape plus a flap on top.

Moving on to a bone bundle hanging from the right hip, mirroring the pouch's position and adding small capsule "bones" with a gradient coloring, attached to a bone joint for rigging purposes.

Writing bone capsule helper...

Building the skull helper...

Rotated boxes pass through rotation via the spread object. Eye sockets use a dark color and poke slightly through the cranium surface, with an optional glow parameter for glowing eyes. Now I'm writing a feather helper function that extrudes a leaf shape with a painted color gradient...

For simplicity I'll skip the vein detail and keep feathers flat-colored to limit the number of painted parts, maybe adding a tip stripe for a two-tone look instead.

For the bandolier I'm adding small spike shapes for the tooth strings, and for the necklace I'm draping a catmull curve around the neck area, considering whether to pull it against the torso surface or define a combined body surface from torso and hump so it sits correctly near the shoulders.

I'm confirming that nesting torso and hump together works as a valid surface target, then sweeping the neck path as a thin leather strand that inherits bone weights from the path itself, and setting up charm placements at several points along the body.

For charms, I'm alternating between a skull amulet with glowing eyes at the midpoint and hanging bone sticks elsewhere, sometimes swapping in a downward spike shaped like a tooth for variety.

Now I'm drafting a bandolier strap draped diagonally across the chest using a catmull curve, then sweeping it into a thick leather band attached to the chest bone.

Adding studs and dangling spikes...

Now I'm positioning the left shoulder pauldron skull, basing it off the shoulder muscle sphere's center and sizing it large with a yaw rotation.

I'm also planning three bone spikes radiating outward from the shoulder muscle's surface, computing their base positions and directions from the shoulder center plus an offset along each spike's direction.

For the shoulders I'm deciding to make them asymmetric Warcraft-style: the left gets a skull pauldron with spikes, while the right gets upward feather plumes plus a crossed bone and smaller spikes, needing a feather helper that can orient upward by swapping its axis parameters.

Now I'm adding elbow spikes jutting outward from a bone joint, a shoulder muscle sphere for bulk, and skipping the redundant upper-arm bulge since the limb radius already covers it. I'm also planning a chest tattoo decal using an SVG spiral-sun texture applied to the torso surface at the hit point.

I'm placing the decal by raycasting from the body's center outward at a forward angle to hit the chest, then adding a second tribal belly-bar decal lower down, while skipping extra face or ear decals since the eyes are already handled with spheres. Writing arm code...

Still writing arm joint logic...

Still defining leg chain...

Adding leather ankle bands and skipping fur boots, then moving on to the head structure with a helper function for positioning relative to the body, starting with the cranium sphere part.

Still refining pupil placement...

Adding a darker eye-socket sphere behind the eyeball for shadowing, then moving on to build the muzzle as a scaled sphere positioned below and forward on the face.

Now I'm placing the nose and nostrils with darker skin tones, adding cheekbone spheres on either side, and constructing the jaw as a tapered frustum box running along the Z-axis for the bone structure.

Still shaping the chin sphere and checking the muzzle-jaw overlap so the closed mouth hides the interior — I'll skip the gum geometry since it's concealed, but I still need to add lower teeth as small cones.

Working out teeth and tusk positions...

Adjusting tusk position slightly to clear the brow and eyes, then adding a gold band ring around the tusks using a torus swept along the tusk path.

I'm also planning smaller accessories: bone stud earrings, ears, and a mohawk. Considering but deciding to skip forehead war-paint decals for simplicity, and thinking about adding a few small wart bumps on the cheeks and nose using small spheres.

Now I'm sketching chin hair as small dark red-orange spikes positioned along the jaw's bottom edge, deciding to skip sideburns, and setting up gradient color bands for the hair.

Writing blade geometry code...

Mane blades on the chest bone follow a similar frustum-box approach, with base positions and lengths still to define.

Now I'm scattering wart details across the torso using small bumpy spheres embedded into the skin, colored a muted olive-green and weighted to body hits. For moss, I'm drawing an SVG texture with several curved green blade strokes to simulate patchy growth on the skin.

I'm sketching a tribal-style tattoo as an SVG: a central ring with radiating lines and diagonal marks, plus a curved underline, sized to render crisply at 256px. I'm also planning a belly marking made of slashes and a zigzag, applied via a decal API that places textures at specific hit points with defined orientation and size.

For the loincloth pattern, I'm designing a procedural paint function that varies by vertical position—trim color near the top, a gold diamond accent partway down, and a mottled leather base elsewhere. For skin, I'm building a layered color function combining counter-shading with mottled green tones to give natural variation.

I'm layering several conditional mixes onto the base skin color: moss patches on the upper back when noise and position align, lighter yellow-green near the top, dark green on the underside, and mud staining near the ground—checking that all these return valid color types. Then I define flat colors for teeth and secondary skin tones, and set up a bone-colored gradient for the tusks based on points along their path.

Now I'm writing a reusable skull-building function that takes a position, joint, scale, yaw rotation, and optional eye color, using a helper to compute rotated local offsets for placing each skull part—cranium, brow ridge, and eye sockets—checking that joint types from the skeleton line up correctly for head, chest, and arm attachments.

I'm verifying the chain configuration so spine, neck, and arm segments have the right number of names matching their joint spans, then moving to assemble shoulder decorations: skull spikes for one side and feather clusters for the other, positioning each piece relative to the shoulder joint.

Writing feather leaf outline function...

Confirming no self-intersections and that the extrude orthogonality constraint holds, I'm placing a skull buckle decoration on the belt and positioning a pouch and cord bundle at the hips for added detail.

Adding more hanging ornaments...

For the back, I'm planning bone fetishes like a crossed-bone backpack with feathers and a skull totem to complete the back silhouette.

Adding placement details...

Good, frame is imported and ring items face outward correctly. Now I need to handle hair/mohawk with a loop, maybe eyebrows too, add a gold shadow tint constant, and double-check for unused variables like av.

Checking that all my helper functions and constants (noise, mottle, gradient, countershade, catmull, glow, mix, smoothstep, resolve, paint, etc.) are actually used so nothing's dangling. Need to verify callback signatures return the right types, confirm the loincloth extrude call takes a color param correctly, and check the surface/ray signature takes origin and direction arrays. Writing the file now, being careful about the import for the along-path helper function.

Setting up the belt as a closed catmull-rom spline from twelve points arranged in a circle around the body. Doing null checks on the tattoo decal, setting eyeball glow strength to 1, keeping the pelvis scale small, and skipping buttocks/hump details -- time to finalize and go.
